short: The Genesis Mission is the federal government's AI for science programme, launched by executive order on 24 November 2025 and run by the Department of Energy across its 17 national laboratories. In July 2026 the White House put more than $5 billion of federal commitments behind it and selected 278 projects. Compute comes from companies: Microsoft's $60 million in July, and National Compute's $100 million in credits reported in October.
title: The Genesis Mission
subtitle: The Department of Energy's national AI for science programme: who runs it, what it has committed, and which companies supply the compute
body_html:
The one-paragraph answer

The Genesis Mission is a federal programme to apply AI to scientific research, created by presidential executive order on 24 November 2025 and led by the Department of Energy through its 17 national laboratories. It is not a regulation and imposes nothing on companies; it is a procurement and research programme, and its relevance to this site is where the compute comes from. On 22 July 2026 the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy announced more than $5 billion in federal commitments, a set of National Science and Technology Challenges, and 278 selected projects. The compute is supplied in part by companies: Microsoft committed $60 million the same day, and on 7 October 2026 Politico reported that National Compute would donate $100 million in computing credits, with the announcement expected on 8 October.

What it is

The executive order Launching the Genesis Mission (24 November 2025) directs the Department of Energy to build a national platform that joins federal supercomputers, scientific datasets and AI models so that researchers can run experiments and simulations at a scale no single laboratory could. DOE calls the platform the American Science and Security Platform. The programme draws on the 17 national laboratories, including the National Nuclear Security Administration laboratories, and on partnerships with AI and chip companies announced at launch.

The July 2026 expansion

On 22 July 2026 OSTP Director Michael Kratsios announced more than $5 billion in federal commitments expanding the Mission. The figure is an aggregate of research awards, funding opportunities, scientific datasets and research facility access committed by more than 15 federal agencies, not a single appropriation. The announcement also named a set of National Science and Technology Challenges, the problems the Mission's projects are organised around.

The Department of Energy selected 278 projects from what it describes as the largest response to a funding opportunity in its history: 168 led by universities, 87 by DOE and NNSA national laboratories, 19 by companies and 4 by non-profits, across 342 institutions in all. Reporting from Nextgov and HPCwire carries the DOE breakdown.

Who supplies the compute

DateCompanyCommitmentSource
2026-07-22Microsoft$60 million: $40 million in Azure compute and AI credits over three years plus $20 million in solution engineering services, coordinated by a new internal office, SPARK, working with the 17 laboratories.Microsoft
2026-10-07National ComputeComputing credits valued at $100 million, reported by Politico ahead of an announcement expected on Thursday 8 October 2026 at an event with Michael Kratsios. The same organisation's name appears on the National Compute Grid, a coalition led by Anjney Midha that launched on 7 October to pool idle AI capacity; this site has not confirmed from a primary source that the two are one organisation.Politico, Axios

Google has also been reported to pledge compute credits, and Nvidia and Anthropic announced partnerships at the November 2025 launch; those are reported by the press and the launch materials rather than confirmed here against a company statement.

Why it belongs beside the data centre registry

Every commitment above is capacity: credits are a claim on someone's data centre. The Mission is therefore one of the larger single public-sector customers for AI compute, and the compute it uses is the same compute that the data centre registry and the GPU availability telemetry on this site track. It also sits inside the federal AI policy picture: see Federal AI Legislation for the executive orders in force and The Politics of AI for who is pushing which way.

Timeline

  • 2025-11-24: Executive order Launching the Genesis Mission; DOE lead; partnerships with AI and chip companies announced.
  • 2026-07-22: OSTP announces more than $5 billion in federal commitments, the National Science and Technology Challenges, and 278 selected projects; Microsoft commits $60 million.
  • 2026-10-07: Politico reports National Compute will donate $100 million in credits; National Compute Grid coalition launches.
  • 2026-10-08: Announcement expected with OSTP Director Kratsios (not yet confirmed at the time of writing).

How this page is kept

Figures are as stated by the White House, DOE and the companies named, with the source beside each. Where a figure comes from press reporting rather than a primary document, the page says so. Updates come from the pipeline's policy news intake, which now queries for the Mission by name.
